title: Poor performance at registering tensors
body:
Hello!

I have been trying to use NIXL as a way to do a sync of my model's parameters across two different NCCL process groups running on two different machines, interconnected via 8 400gbs infiniband NICs. The typical HGX 8xH100 setup.

I found that NIXL is taking a very long time in registering the tensors to memory; effectively prohibitively slow.

Here is a simple repro with the 125M GPT-2 model:
```
import torch
import time
from nixl._api import nixl_agent, nixlBind
from transformers import GPT2Config, GPT2LMHeadModel

device = "cuda"

def run_weight_sync_test():
    config = GPT2Config()
    with torch.device("meta"):
        model = GPT2LMHeadModel(config)
    torch.manual_seed(0)

    model.to_empty(device=device)
    with torch.no_grad():
        model.init_weights()
    
    agent = nixl_agent("test", None)
    for i in range(8):
        agent.nixl_mems["cuda:" + str(i)] = nixlBind.VRAM_SEG

    # print parameter count
    print(f"Parameter count: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()):,}")
    
    tensors = [p for p in model.parameters()]
    start = time.perf_counter()
    for i, tensor in enumerate(tensors):
        reg_desc = agent.get_reg_descs(tensor)
        print(f"Registering memory for tensor {i}")
        assert agent.register_memory(reg_desc) is not None
    end = time.perf_counter()
    print(f"Time taken: {end - start:.2f} seconds")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    torch.cuda.set_device(0)
    run_weight_sync_test()
```

On my machine it takes 50.47 seconds to register the tensors. In production, I use a model much much larger than 100M, which can take almost an hour to register the tensors.

I'm using CUDA 12.6 and a build of UCX 1.18.0, configured with the following flags:
```
./configure \
        --prefix=<ucx install path> \
        --enable-shared \
        --disable-static \
        --disable-doxygen-doc \
        --enable-optimizations \
        --enable-cma \
        --enable-devel-headers \
        --with-go=no \
        --with-verbs \
        --with-dm \
        --with-cuda="/usr/local/cuda-12.6/" \
        --enable-mt \
        --with-mlx5-dv
make -j 
make -j install-strip
ldconfig
```

I also run UCX with the `UCX_TLS=^cuda_ipc` env var, mimicking the Dynamo setup.

Thank you!
author: cassanof

comments.body:
Hi,
Thank you for trying out NIXL!

When registering descriptors with the agent you can pass them as a _**list**_ of (1) tuples or (2) torch tensors. You can also pass NIXL descriptors if you call `get_reg_descs` beforehand.

The problem is that you are passing a single tensor which was sliced to many elements. We will add more documentation for clarification and add support for handling a single tensor efficiently.

By changing the code to:
```
agent.register_memory([tensor])
```
the overall registration time drops from ~24 seconds to ~2.5ms. `register_memory` will take care of `reg_descs` for you.

If you want to cut the registration time even further, you can actually pass the entire tensor list without iterating over it in python.
```
reg_descs = agent.register_memory(tensors)
assert reg_descs is not None
agent.deregister_memory(reg_descs)
```
This drops the overall registration time to ~1ms.

If that is not fast enough, for each contiguous memory region  you can provide a base address, length and device ID as a tuple for a single registration. Note that with UCX (or any RDMA backend) every registration involves a system call, pinning the pages and mapping them to the kernel's DMA subsystem.

Ohhhh, I see what's going on. 
Thank you so much for clarifying. This library is great! Happy to be an early adopter.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of why tensor registration is slow in the user's code
A more efficient approach to register tensors with NIXL
Clear code examples demonstrating the correct usage pattern
Information about NIXL's API design and intended usage patterns

title: Question: what does `sorted` mean in  `nixlRegDList`?
body:
PR title.
Wondering when I should set `sorted` to true or false.

Thanks!
author: cassanof

comments.body:
If nixlXferDlist is sorted, it can benefit from some perf optimization when creating a handle. We kept it for nixlRegDlist, just as they have the same base class and we wanted to be consistent, but it doesn't provide any perf boost. We were debating to remove it from the python interface, just kept it for consistency reasons for now. Because even the slight possible perf improvement is not that useful, it's just during initialization and for a few memory regions. What you see in the test was just to make sure passing of optional arguments and so are working properly. We might update the test a little bit not to be misleading.

Aside from that, when submitting a transfer, if the nixlXferDlist is sorted, since the internal registered memory lists are also sorted, we can find the relevant information for each descriptor in linear time instead of NlogM, N being number of elements in the XferDList and M being number of registered memories for that specific backend and that memory type.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of the purpose and effect of the 'sorted' parameter in nixlRegDList
Information about the practical impact of using the 'sorted' parameter
Context about why the parameter exists in the API
Guidance on when to use each option (true/false)

title: blocking_send_recv_example.py seems incorrect
body:
Hello! Firstly, this library looks extremely promising, would solve a very big issue I was dealing with!

I had a look at the `blocking_send_recv_example.py` to see how I could potentially send over a tensor.
This test doesn't seem to work, it misuses `zmq`, as both procs are doing `connect`, while the correct usage is for the target proc to use `.bind` and the initiator proc to use `.connect`. The string literal for the addr in `.connect` is also wrong as there are a few extra spaces.

After fixing a few of these issues myself, I am getting the following error from the initiator:
```

Would be great if there was a functional example on how to send over a tensor 🙏
author: cassanof

comments.body:
Hello and thanks for pointing this out. We have fixed it in PR #65 and it's already merged. We further added data checks and some clean ups to the code.
 
One point to consider is that two sided and blocking is not our targeted mode of operation, this was an example to give an idea of how it's possible to replicate 2-sided with 1-sided. (Since it was an example to demonstrate the idea, it was supposed to be in our examples directory, and we plan to add CIs for examples directory very soon to avoid these issues). You can still pass tensors to 1-sided operations too, it's the same API.

thank you! 

i got it to work last night. been a big unblocker for me. thanks for releasing this library!
